notes: Round 1 of the arc side of the kitted-curve loop, against Checkpoint C (measured after shaped WELDED patch pieces, boost bays, catalog surgery, gridlock chip; kit-less unchanged from baseline). Day 1 gets no item: kitted delta over kit-less is already +0.0 there and design intent says not to chase it. Lever priority this round: patchDrop first wherever cells/win is material (it is kit-less-neutral, since the kit-less proxy is rotation-only and never touches patches), then slag as the shared structural lever, then small greed nudges bounded by known kit-less calibration (~0.5-0.9 pts per 0.01), with oppRam deliberately withheld at D4-D8 (the lever that overshot ~10 pts/point at D6-D8 in the original balance loop's Round 1) and spent only once, at D9, where kit-less headroom is largest. Grid/minCost growth begins at D9 and lands hardest at the finale, per the user's waiver on 'grid almost never' for this pass. RECOMMENDATION: pull the ability-agent's hotBoot +2->+1 sim-gated candidate into round 1 alongside these deltas. Evidence: the kit's advantage over kit-less jumps from +0.0 at day 1 (no boosts) to +16.5 at day 2, the exact day hotBoot@2 activates and the day before patches or mode pairs exist to explain it; and the finale round-1-kill math (opening RAM 9 + hotBoot +2 = 11 rotation RAM turn 1) names hotBoot specifically as a term in the closability inequality. Arc levers (abilityFreq, greed) can only blunt the downstream symptom at day 2; they cannot touch the root cause the way a boost-value tone-down can, and every day from 2 onward inherits whatever hotBoot leaves unfixed.

items.rationale: FLAG: charter rule reserves finale changes for explicit user sign-off; this item exists because BRIEF.md scopes it explicitly ('a finale package with an explicit parFlat... HARD GATE: zero round-1 finale closes') as a user-locked decision for this cycle. Confirm before integration regardless. ROUND-1-KILL REASONING: Checkpoint C finale kitted is 80.5 vs target 48 (+32.5), with round-1 closes at 107 of 161 wins (66.5%) and the highest cells/win in the game. The kitted profile opens with 9 rotation RAM; hotBoot@2 adds +2, giving 11 RAM available on turn 1. At the current finale minCost 24 with headStart 4 (4 nodes of the route already pre-completed at dive start) on a 13x11 grid, the remaining route is short enough that 11 RAM closes it in a single turn most of the time, even with only a shortcut cross piece in hand. This is a route-length problem, not a win-rate problem, so it needs structural levers: (1) grid 13x11 -> 15x13, the single largest jump in the whole table, lengthening minimum node-to-node distances; (2) minCost 24 -> 30 (+6, 25% higher, the largest minCost jump in the curve); (3) headStart 4 -> 2, removing 2 nodes of pre-completed progress so more of the now-longer route remains open at turn 1 rather than less. These three together should push the turn-1-affordable fraction of the route well below what 11 RAM buys, independent of any win-rate lever. Secondary, non-structural contributions stacked on top: oppRam 10 -> 11 (+1, general resistance, unmeasured for kitted), abilityFreq 0.8 -> 0.85 (more opponent counters against a fully maxed kit), and slag 0.18 -> 0.27 (+0.09, denser board means the finale's 3 patch pieces cover a smaller share of the now-longer route, directly targeting the cells/win 0.35-0.89 pattern). Also setting an explicit parFlat of 0, replacing the current default (constant PAR_FLAT=2), which the brief flags as an existing inconsistency: 2 is looser than day 9's parFlat of 1, and the finale should be the tightest margin in the game, not the loosest. NOTE ON THE INVERSION: finale headStart (2) now sits below day 9's (4) by design. This is the one dimension deliberately decoupled from the day9-to-finale escalation because it is the specific lever the round-1-kill needs; the grid, minCost, oppRam, and slag jumps carry the 'father's machine, hardest fight in the game' framing instead, and together they leave the finale harder than day 9 on every other axis. This is a conservative first-round structural move: if round-1 closes are not fully at zero after remeasurement, the next lever to pull is a further headStart cut (to 0 or 1) or a further minCost increase, in that order, before touching grid size again.
